claims.text: The lane-1 outcome reported in an assessment is a copy of the headline outcome, passed in as a finished value; no code computes a lane-1 outcome from lane-1 facts.
boundary: src/aee/lanes.py build_lanes and its single call site in src/aee/engine.py on main at 8211643

evidence.description: build_lanes receives outcome as a parameter and places it verbatim at lanes.lane_1.outcome; per-claim lane-1 score facts exist but no lane-1 outcome logic exists.
The engine calls build_lanes with outcome set to the already-demoted headline outcome, so lane 1 can never differ from the headline.

falsification_tests: Show code that computes a lane-1 outcome from failures and scores separately from the headline outcome.

claims.text: A bundle whose machine checking is fully clean still cannot reach headline pass while any claim is a draft or below the explained stage, because the outcome logic routes both states to iterate after every machine check has passed.

evidence.description: After the failure and score steps, any draft claim returns iterate (the draft cap), and any claim below stage explained returns iterate (the stage rule).
Draft-cap failures are outcome-bearing by design, and the stage module records that the lane-qualified outcome form was deferred and never built.

falsification_tests: Show a bundle with a draft claim or a claim below stage explained, clean machine checks, and all scores at or above 0.70 that reaches headline pass.

claims.text: The gate recomputes only the headline outcome from an assessment file and never reads the lanes record, so a forged lane-1 outcome in the file is not detected.

evidence.description: The cross-check recomputes the headline from claims, scores, summary counts, threshold, verdicts, stage caps, and the ledger; the word lanes does not appear in the gate path.
Every gate forgery test targets the headline outcome, scores, or the ledger; none forges a lane value, because the gate has no lane check to catch it.
